title: DOST explores Carabao mango as space food

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The Department of Science and Technology–Philippine Nuclear Research Institute (DOST-PNRI) is exploring how to develop Carabao mango into food for long-duration space missions.
The project is set to be featured at the National Science, Technology, and Innovation Week (NSTW) on November 25 to 29, 2026, in General Santos City, South Cotabato.

The Philippine Space Mango Program brings together DOST-PNRI, the University of the Philippines Diliman for food science expertise, the Philippine Space Agency, and the Batangas Mango High Value Growers Agriculture Cooperative (BAMAHGACO) as a partner in mango production.

A taste of home in space

“We’re taking the Carabao mango and exploring how it can be part of the Filipino story in space,” said Gina B. Abrera of DOST-PNRI, the program’s project leader in a press release. “We want a product that can travel far, represent our identity, and remind future astronauts of home.”
Beyond its nutritional value, the project aims to give future Filipino astronauts a familiar taste of home as the country works toward sending its first astronaut to space by 2035.
“We’re not just thinking about nutrition. We’re thinking about identity, comfort, and home,” Abrera added.

Aside from its potential use in space missions, the project is also expected to help strengthen the Philippine dried mango industry’s competitiveness in international markets and explore food solutions for emergencies and disaster response.

NSTW is DOST’s annual celebration of the country’s scientific and technological achievements, bringing together researchers, industry representatives, government agencies, and academic institutions to showcase homegrown innovations.
